statement: There is an ineffective X_0 such that for every X >= X_0 and every interval I of consecutive odd integers contained in [X, 2X] with |I| = floor((2/3) X^{1/3}), the values floor(x^{3/2}) for x in I are not all of one parity. This is Paper B Lemmas 3.2–3.4 (parity bridge, van der Corput second-derivative, Erdős–Turán) localized to the hug-flow working window: g(r) = (1/2)(2r+1)^{3/2} has g'' ≍ X^{-1/2} uniformly on the dyadic block, the h-th mode is ≪ H h^{1/2} X^{-1/4} + h^{-1/2} X^{1/4}, and cutoff K = X^{1/6} gives absolute discrepancy D ≪ X^{1/6} + X^{1/4} = o(H). No resonance exclusion is used (first-derivative locking lengthens sojourns but does not shrink g''). Not a depth-2 statement, not C_L nonempty, not a transfer theorem, not a Paper B edit, and not a halt theorem.
